# Hyprland notes

Facts about the Hyprland 0.56 Lua dispatch API (`hyprctl dispatch "hl.dsp...."`) that its output does not state. Found by trying them; re-check after a Hyprland upgrade.

- **Try new calls on a spare window.** A dispatch that goes wrong can leave a window changed for good: a test that faded a window left it at an explicit opacity until it was reopened.
- **Window properties** (`hl.dsp.window.set_prop({ prop, value, window })`): the names are `opacity`, `opacity_inactive`, `opacity_fullscreen`, not `alpha`. There is no way to unset one: `"unset"` and `""` fail with `stof`, and `-1` makes the window invisible. Setting `"1"` is the closest to a reset, and it overrides the user's opacity rules.
- **Maximize and full screen**: `hl.dsp.window.fullscreen({ mode = "maximized" | "fullscreen", action = "set" | "unset" | "toggle", window = "address:0x..." })`. `hyprctl -j clients` reports it as `fullscreen`: 0 none, 1 maximized, 2 full screen. With the `scrolling` layout a maximized window can sit beside others instead of covering them.
- **Focus**: `hl.dsp.focus({ window = "address:0x..." })`, `hl.dsp.focus({ monitor = "DP-1" })` and `hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = "3" })`. Focusing a window on a hidden workspace switches that monitor to it. `misc:on_focus_under_fullscreen` decides what a focus request does to a covering window.
- **Pointer**: focusing can warp the pointer. Wrap it in `hyprctl eval 'hl.config({ cursor = { no_warps = true } })'` and put the old value back (see `focusWindow` in `DockHyprland.js`).
- **Reading state**: `hyprctl -j clients`, `monitors` (each has `activeWorkspace.id`) and `activewindow`.
- **Private state in helper processes**: taskbar focus and preview rescue read client and monitor snapshots through anonymous pipes with `jq -s ... <(hyprctl -j clients) <(hyprctl -j monitors)`. Passing snapshots through `--argjson` exposes window titles and other metadata in process arguments. Only the validated window address, static filter, and pipe descriptor paths belong in the rescue command's arguments. The executable regressions cover focus, focus with pointer warp, and preview recovery using synthetic metadata.
- **Raising**: `hl.dsp.focus` focuses a floating window without raising it, so one under another floating window is focused but hidden. `hl.dsp.window.alter_zorder({ mode = "top", window = "address:0x..." })` raises it (see `RAISE` in `DockHyprland.js`).
- **Moving the pointer**: `hl.dsp.cursor.move` alone does not make Hyprland follow it with focus, and does not trigger a hover on the Dock or its Previews. Real motion does, so `scripts/pointer.sh move X Y` warps and then nudges 1 px with `ydotool`, and `left` / `right` click. That needs `ydotool` and a writable `/dev/uinput` (`sudo modprobe uinput`; `echo uinput | sudo tee /etc/modules-load.d/uinput.conf` so it loads at boot; then a udev rule giving `wheel` mode 0660: `KERNEL=="uinput", SUBSYSTEM=="misc", GROUP="wheel", MODE="0660", OPTIONS+="static_node=uinput"` in `/etc/udev/rules.d/80-uinput.rules`, and `sudo udevadm trigger --action=change --subsystem-match=misc --sysname-match=uinput`; `uaccess` does not work for `uinput`); the daemon it starts is not a service. Warping to the bottom edge reveals an auto-hidden Dock. Keys go to the focused window, and a stray Escape closed a TUI settings window of the user's: send them with `scripts/pointer.sh key`, which refuses unless a throwaway window is focused, never with `ydotool key`.
- **Preview menu**: it ignores Escape. It closes on an outside click, or once the pointer has been on it and leaves.
- **Focus after a Preview click**: with the Preview closing under a pointer that is over another floating window, Hyprland's `follow_mouse` hands focus to that window about 10 ms after our `focus`, though the clicked window is raised and shown. Focus calls from a shell do not do this. Not solved: a second `focus` 150 ms later is reverted the same way. Accepted for now: the Window is raised and shown, but the one under the pointer is the highlighted one.
- **Finding who changed focus**: explicitly run `scripts/hypr-events.sh start`, reproduce by hand, read `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/startbar-events.log`, then run `scripts/hypr-events.sh stop`. The runtime directory must be absolute, owned by the current user and mode `0700`. Logs and PID state use mode `0600`; custom log paths are passed literally. Events can contain private window titles, so keep exported logs private. Existing exports are not changed by updating the tool. It keeps its PID in a file because `pkill -f` matches the shell that runs it and kills it.
- **A spare window to test on**: `scripts/spare.sh open` prints its address, `state ADDR` shows its workspace, full screen state and floating, `close ADDR` closes it and goes back to your workspace. Float or move it with `hl.dsp.window.float({ action = "set", ... })` and `hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = "2", follow = false, ... })`. Launching the user's own apps to see what they do opens windows on their session.
- **Omarchy's workspace modes** (`/usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/workspace-modes.lua`): on a floating-mode workspace Omarchy floats every window and tags it `omarchy-mode-floated` (`hyprctl -j clients` lists `tags`), so a floating window is not necessarily a dialog: a dialog has no such tag. Omarchy minimizes a window to `special:minimized`. A spare window opens floating there; `float` with `action = "off"` tiles it.
- **A setting acts live.** A plugin setting in `~/.config/omarchy/shell.json` applies to the running shell at once, so a hook such as `newWindowWorkspace` also acts on a spare window. To try its script alone, set the key to `off` first and put `shell.json` back from a copy afterwards.
- **Screenshots**: `grim -o DP-1 file.png` takes one monitor; a bare `grim` takes both side by side at twice the width. `grim -o` and `-g` cannot be combined: crop with `magick`.
- **Windows outside every monitor** (workaround, revisit if Hyprland or Omarchy stops leaving them): a floating window keeps its coordinates when the monitor it was on goes away, so it can sit where no monitor is. Seen with `monitors.lua` placing DP-1 at 0x0 and DP-3 at 1920x0 and only DP-3 connected: two Edge web-app windows at x=362 and x=410, `mapped`, not `hidden`, tagged `omarchy-mode-floated`. Focusing them switches workspace and shows only the wallpaper, and their Preview thumbnails are blank, since there is nothing on screen to capture. `rescue` in `DockHyprland.js` (run by `focusWindow` and `focusWindowAndWarp`, so a Dock Item click, a Preview click and the Pick after a peek, and by `rescueWindows` when a Preview opens) centers a floating window with less than 64x32 layout px on any monitor, using `hl.dsp.window.center`; it leaves tiled windows alone. `hl.dsp.window.float` toggles whatever `action` says, so check `floating` in `hyprctl -j clients` after calling it. Not reproduced from scratch (unplug a monitor with floating windows on it) and not reported upstream.
